page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor under the x86_64 architecture. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 32 vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, clocked up to 3.525 GHz. Memory configuration comprises 128.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Premium Storage capabilities, while operating without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core computational execution, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 2712.77 in the top 25% tier. PassMark memory testing ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2898.2, alongside uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 77.67 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 44.95 GB/sec. Multi-core performance scales predictably across 32 threads, returning 43242.33 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12743.0, both settling within the middle 50% percentile.

Hardware instruction set support covers AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations, alongside BMI2 and FMA extensions, while omitting AVX-512 extensions and AMX tiles. This architecture delivers consistent results for data compression, showing 25.81 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 155.48 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In-memory data store performance reaches 31.76 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, while web server throughput sustains 24.55 GB/sec.

The inclusion of 1288 GB of direct-attached local SSD reduces dependency on remote storage for scratch spaces, local caches, and temporary tables. Without integrated hardware acceleration, large language model prompt evaluation for 70B models drops into the lower 25% percentile, reflecting the architectural tradeoff of CPU-bound machine learning tasks versus dedicated accelerators. The configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency by balancing balanced CPU-to-memory density with integrated high-capacity local SSD for enterprise web serving, relational databases, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. Designed on an x86_64 architecture running on Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The server includes 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage and operates without dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core compute performance and memory throughput in the top 25% percentile, while multi-core workloads, such as Clang compilation and multi-threaded decompression, fall in the mid-range 50%. Incorporating hardware encryption and vector extensions, the instance provides high resource density and local storage capacity. It is suited for relational database systems, distributed caching tiers, enterprise application backends, and intensive software compilation pipelines.
